title: tenant-graceful-degrade-orchestrator-and-telemetry-connectors-for-5xx-waves
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary:
High-severity customer escalations (T-1254, T-1298, internal alert cluster during 2026-03-08) exposed a pattern where tenant bursts cause short-lived 5xx amplification across hosted frontdoors. Contributing factors: uncoordinated retries from SDKs, synchronous fanout to dedicated variants, and transient kvcache churn that increases p99 latency and triggers backend timeouts.

Goals:
- Implement a tenant-scoped graceful-degrade orchestrator that can: (a) detect tenant-level 5xx amplification signals, (b) apply lightweight per-tenant admission limits and backoff policies, and (c) route to safe degraded models or cached responses when appropriate.
- Add telemetry connectors and dashboards to observe the orchestrator decisions and customer-visible error rates.
- Ship a phased rollout with canary + progressive ramp to avoid collateral impact.

Design notes / approach:
1) Signal surface: combine three signals into a short-circuit score: recent 5xx rate (1m/5m windows), KV cache eviction spikes, and connection-hold ratio. Thresholds are conservative for initial rollout to avoid false positives.
2) Admission controller: token-bucket per-tenant with dynamic depletion on 5xx spikes. Tokens can be reclaimed by lowering batch sizes or switching to cached prefix responses.
3) Transparent fallback: integrate with routing layer to optionally route degraded traffic to either (A) a small warm model variant (quantized) or (B) an immediately-returned cached prefix where applicable. We will prefer (B) for deterministic prompt families to preserve semantics.
4) Retry harmonization: override SDK-level immediate retries by injecting a server-side retry-coalescer header that informs clients (via SDK update) of suggested backoff windows for that tenant.
5) Observability: new Datadog/Grafana metrics (tenant.5xx_score, tenant.admission_drops, tenant.fallback_rate), tracing tags, and a dedicated dashboard for oncall with per-tenant heatmap and last-decision trace link.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong per-tenant throttles risk customer QoS regression; we prioritized gentle admission with fallback first.
- Routing to quantized variants may change output fidelity; fallback is limited to tenants with >60% non-deterministic prompts only after customer notification.
- Server-side retry guidance requires SDK adoption; initial value is advisory and we do server-side dampening in parallel so SDK updates are not strictly required.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: 1% of traffic split across 20 tenants (selected low-risk customers) for 72h, monitor correctness metrics and customer tickets.
- Progressive ramp: 10% after clean canary, then 50% with ability to abort.
- Full roll: enable by default with opt-out within 2 weeks.

Acceptance criteria:
- per-tenant 5xx amplification events reduced by >=60% within 5 minutes of admission action on canary tenants (compare to baseline).
- No increase in end-to-end error SLA on non-targeted tenants during canary (<=1% delta).
- Dashboard and trace links available; oncall can trigger immediate rollback within 5 minutes.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RW/tenant-graceful-degrade-orchestrator
- PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4587
- PR (edge-router): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/122
- Datadog dashboard: https://dd.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant-5xx-orchestrator
- Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/tenant-orchestrator
- Incident write-up (root cause): https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-03-08-5xx-wave

Notes: this ticket focuses on the runtime + routing + telemetry pieces. SDK advisory header rollout tracked separately (PM-2201).
